doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Where Wild Man On The Loose came from
summary: He got the idea from a man just in from the country, not a particular friend.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I got the idea for that...I was playing at Sugar Hill in ‘60. I think it was after ‘60... But
that’s the first time I played there. I don’t know how much later was it...
How did you come to write “Wild Man On The Loose.” “Look out, stand back...” What were you... It wasn’t him.
Bill Patey(?—34:08), you used to call him...his nickname was “Wild Man.”
It was a compilation, I think, of people of a certain type that we all know.
No. I got the idea from a guy who had spent several weeks in the country, and...
Well, it says that in this note. He’d been in the country for 30 days...
Yeah. “Been in the country for 30 days, got some money, got some hell to raise...”
Something about “looking up that juice” or something...
“Soaking up that juice.” Anyway, we have a friend who says that’s his theme song.
Well, I don’t know when that was written, but...
